text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: `CLOUD-AZ1-GPU-EVICTIONS` — sustained KV cache evictions + 5xx surge for model-serving in az1. Severity: P1. Link: https://pd.example.com/alerts/CLOUD-AZ1-GPU-EVICTIONS

pagerduty: Alert triggered for service: inference-runtime (policy: az1-eviction-threshold). Escalation policy: oncall-sre -> eng-lead.

sarah: I'm on it, acked the PD alert. Seeing the same on Grafana, eviction rate jumped ~300% at 12:04 UTC. Rolling deploys look fine, this smells like noisy eviction storms on one GPU pool.

raj: I pulled kube events from az1 cluster: lots of OOMKilled on pod sidecars, then liveness restarts. Suspect misbehaving batching jobs + KV mem pressure.

maya: Request routing shows ~15% of traffic still hitting az1 despite fallback policy. Router logs: `route_decision: prefer_az_same_region` then `fallback=false` for some customer tiers.

leo: Quick mitigation proposal: 1) enable immediate model routing fallback for hosted API to prefer az2/az3 2) scale up warm standby in az2 by +20 GPUs 3) mark az1 as degraded in Console so canary rollouts avoid it. Anyone object?

sarah: doing (1) now — flipping routing flag to allow cross-az fallback for all tier types.

maya: I pushed the routing change, config id `cfg-az1-fallback-2026-04-12`. Confirming LB is rebalancing.

raj: I started draining non-essential worker pods in az1 to reduce churn. Command: `kubectl label nodes az1-* cordon=true && kubectl drain node --ignore-daemonsets` (running slowly).

incident-bot: User-impact assessment: 47 distinct customers reported elevated errors in the last 10 minutes, concentrated on EU-west region. Estimated affected qps: 420 -> baseline 260.

sarah: Noting customer impact: model-completions return 502/504; embeddings and async jobs mostly unaffected. Sending priority email to ops-supp so CS can triage active sessions.

leo: I'm activating failover playbook step 3: warmfailover -> route primary traffic to az2 until eviction rate normalizes. Trigger: `playbook/failover-az1-warm-2026-04-12`

pagerduty: sarah acknowledged. Escalating to eng-lead (leo) due to cross-AZ impact.

oncall-manager: handoff note — current oncall (sarah) will keep ownership for incident stabilization, then hand off to night-oncall (raj) in 30 minutes. Please update runbook.

maya: Confirming traffic shift: az1 serving qps down 60%, az2 qps up accordingly. 5xx rate in az1 decreasing but KV eviction still high.

raj: I've identified a runaway batch worker in az1 doing large mem allocations every minute. Killed the offending pod, monitoring for recurrence. Logs: ```0:12:06 batch_worker: allocate 3.2GB -> eviction triggered
0:12:07 kvcache: evict key=xyz size=1.2MB```

sarah: Good catch. Also we should rotate the routing rule back once kv eviction < 10/min and 5xx rate < 0.5%.

leo: I'll keep the failover active for 20 minutes, then we validate and do controlled re-enable. Preparing incident summary for postmortem: root cause hypotheses, mitigation timeline, customer-impact list, and follow-ups (rate-limits on batch jobs, better eviction alerts).

pagerduty: Incident resolved: after mitigations, az1 eviction rate returned to baseline at 12:34 UTC. PD alert automatically closed.

sarah: marking incident as resolved in Slack. Adding notes to runbook: add a preflight to detect runaway batching, add automatic fallback for cross-az by default when evictions > threshold.

oncall-manager: handoff complete — raj will pick up the follow-ups. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
